title: Apple bets on new screen gadget, Siri AI in home device push
source_used: Reuters, read on its wire copy at Euronext (live.euronext.com); same text cross-checked on BNN Bloomberg
key_facts: Apple launched HomeView on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, an iPad-like smart display that starts at $299 and starts shipping next month (Reuters).
It has a 7-inch screen and face recognition and helps users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks (Reuters).
Apple said the device will not be sold in the European Union because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations.
To pull in private data from messages and calendars, HomeView relies on a recently unlocked iPhone on the same home network.

Apple also updated HomePod and Apple TV and introduced doorbells, cameras and thermostats made by LG and Schneider Electric with Apple's help; the new Apple TV 4K starts at $299, more than double its predecessor.

Analysts quoted: PP Foresight's Paolo Pescatore says Apple must show its AI delivers real benefits; Apple upgraded Siri this summer with help from Google, and it is unclear whether it is competitive enough.
Comparison prices: Amazon Echo Show 8 $199.99, Google Nest Hub $99.99.
Apple shares rose about 1% after earlier touching a record.
quote_evidence: The HomeView device, which starts at $299 and starts shipping next month, is Apple's latest entry into a highly competitive market for connected home devices.
The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said.

Apple this summer upgraded Siri's capabilities with assistance from Google but analysts said it is unclear whether its AI assistant is competitive enough to lure consumers to a crowded connected home device space.
why_it_matters_hint: Apple is betting its upgraded Siri can win a home-device market where it has had little success, and EU buyers are excluded.
